newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says peso to remain market-determined.
newsitem.headline: Manila says peso to remain market-determined.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Thursday the peso will remain market-dertermined despite calls for its devaluation.
"Our firm commitment today to a market-determined exchange rate is wisdom learned from long and bitter experience," Singson said in a speech during the Central Bank's fourth anniversary.
"Recently, there were again calls to engineer a devaluation and to fix the exchange rate allegedly to boost our competitiveness," he said.
"However, we have gone through these routes and other artificial exchange rate fixing experiments before with invariably disappointing results and failed expectations."
Exporters have been urging the Central Bank to let the peso depreciate to make them more competitive.
On Wednesday, speculators trained their eyes on the peso, hoping it would succumb to depreciation after Thailand's de facto devaluation.
Investors had been drawing comparisons between the Philippines and Thailand because both have a current account deficit and an overheating property sector.
The Central Bank quickly moved to restore calm on Wednesday by raising its overnight rate to 24 percent and selling dollars heavily.

Singson noted the peso exchange rate moved by only a few centavos, depreciating by less than one-half of one percent over the past 12 months despite some recent major external financial disturbances in the region.
